official.name: Alan and Jane Handler Endowed Scholarship

verification.funding_note: The award equals the full cost of attendance (no fixed dollar value is published). The published fixed components are an enrichment fund of up to $5,000 over the four-year program and a $100-per-year academic supply grant.
verification.funding_period: Four years; enrichment fund over four years
verification.covered_expenses: Tuition, fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation for the four-year academic program (health insurance covered if applicable); up to $5,000 enrichment fund for summer school, academic or professional endeavors, or study abroad; individual mentoring and academic support; special alumni network.
eligibility: First-year, fall-term domestic and international applicants; transfer and spring applicants are not eligible
Substantial levels of financial need demonstrated on the CSS Profile and FAFSA
High school and independent counselors, teachers, and community-based organization officials may nominate; nominations from students or parents are not accepted
Selection on academic excellence, outstanding potential to be future leaders, and demonstrated mastery of complex challenges
required_docs: University of Rochester first-year application (Early Decision not required; should be submitted by December 1)
Financial aid documents - CSS Profile and, where applicable, FAFSA
Nomination submitted by a counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official (Sept 15 - Nov 30)
No additional Handler-specific materials required; all first-year applicants are reviewed
verification.deadline_note: Counselor nominations open September 15 and close November 30; the application should be submitted by December 1 (not required to be Early Decision). Finalists are announced in mid-February and must attend the mandatory two-part virtual interview event; renewal requires applying for financial aid annually by March 15.
verification.application_process: A counselor, teacher, or community-based organization nominates the student through the Rochester nomination portal. All University of Rochester first-year applicants are then automatically reviewed for the scholarship simply by submitting an application and completing necessary financial aid documents; finalists are invited to a virtual interview in mid-February.
verification.contact_info: Office of Admissions, admit@admissions.rochester.edu, (585) 275-3221; Karin Wilson, Handler Scholarship Program Director, karin.wilson@rochester.edu
verification.interview_requirement: Yes; selected finalists must participate in the mandatory two-part virtual interview event in mid-February.
verification.status_note: Verified on admissions.rochester.edu/handler-scholarship, retrieved 2026-10-10. International students are eligible (FAQ: international students will be selected each year, and the current scholar cohort includes students from Zimbabwe, the Dominican Republic, Syria & Italy, and Uruguay). The program was established by Rich and Martha Handler in 2007 with an ultimate commitment of $25 million. The University's page gives month-day dates without a year; December 1 (2026-12-01) is used for the current cycle, and confirmation should be obtained from the Office of Admissions.

applicant_utility.exciting_but_honest_wins: The Handler covers the whole cost of attending Rochester for four years - tuition, mandatory fees, housing, food, books, personal and transportation costs - and hands you up to $5,000 more to spend on the summer that will define your résumé: research, internships or study abroad. Royalties on top include individual mentoring, a $100 annual book grant, and access to the Handler alumni network. The current cohort includes scholars from Zimbabwe, the Dominican Republic, Syria, Italy and Uruguay, so this is demonstrably not a domestic-only pipeline.
applicant_utility.good_fit_if: You are a first-year applicant (fall entry, not transfer) with real financial need who has already pushed through obstacles the admissions office can see: family disruption, caregiving, refugee or immigration experience, work alongside school, or an under-resourced school. It fits if a counselor, teacher or community organization leader knows your story well enough to nominate you - you cannot self-nominate - and if your academic record backs the leadership narrative.
applicant_utility.potential_drawbacks: Everything rides on a nomination from someone else, and if no adult in your orbit nominates you, you are invisible to this process. The February interview is mandatory, so an extenuating travel issue needs early communication. Renewal is conditional on Satisfactory Academic Progress and annual FAFSA filing by March 15, and the scholarship does not cover optional extras like dining flex, parking or dorm damage charges.
document_checklist: Nomination submitted by a counselor/teacher/community organization official between September 15 and November 30
University of Rochester application (Common App) by December 1
CSS Profile and, if eligible, FAFSA completed by the financial aid office
Interview availability for the mid-February virtual finalist event
By the following March 15, annual financial aid renewal application
applicant_utility.playbook_for_working_applicants: Find your nominator in September, not December: the window closes November 30, and the strongest nominations come from people who can describe a specific obstacle you navigated, not a general recommendation. Brief your counselor with a one-page summary of your circumstances and goals so the nomination is concrete. Submit the Rochester application by December 1 even under Regular Decision, and file the CSS Profile and FAFSA at the same time because need is assessed from them. Treat the mid-February interview as a conversation about resilience and what you will do with the support, and keep a running list of how you would use the $5,000 enrichment fund - study abroad, a summer research assistantship, or an unpaid internship - since that answer is where finalists can differentiate.
